text:
anna: Heads-up — regression in nightly serving tests. After KV-cache warmup (lots of prefix hits) + CUDA graph capture enabled, we get apparent serialization across GPUs. nvprof shows repeated cross-stream waits. Repro and logs below.

kevin: Ugh, saw a perf sniff last night but didn’t track the graph interaction. Any chance it’s a stream leak or we’re capturing wrong stream? :thinking: 

miguel: Can you paste the nvprof / nvtx output? Also which graph capture mode (thread, stream) are we using?

anna: Using per-inference stream capture via cudaStreamBeginCapture(stream, CUDA_STREAM_CAPTURE_MODE_GLOBAL). We thought global capture would be safe for async memcpys and nccl.

anna: Profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
Stream 0: kernel LAYER_FWD_1 (grid 256)
Stream 1: kernel KV_LOOKUP (grid 64)
Stream 7: cudaMemcpyAsync (host->device)
Event 123: Stream 0 waiting on Stream 7
Event 124: Stream 1 waiting on Stream 7
NCCL AllReduce queued on Stream 0, then waits for Stream 7
Repeated pattern every step after warmup (approx step 40)
```

jen: If the graph capture is capturing the memcpy stream as a dependency, when instantiated it might serialize access to that stream across GPUs. That would explain the sudden jump in per-step latency after warmup (when memcpy pattern stabilizes).

kevin: Also noticed the KV cache warmup changes memory traffic patterns — more host pinned memcpy for cache fills early, then steady small async copies later. Graph capture might be coalescing those and forcing global sync.

miguel: Did you try disabling graph capture to confirm? Perf-bot?

perf-bot: nightly-serving-regression: baseline (no-graph) p50=85ms, with-graph p50=210ms, p99 spikes to 800ms. Regression triggers after ~40 steps in our harness.

anna: Yes, disabling graph capture returns perf to baseline. So it's definitely capture-related. But we need graphs for throughput.

kevin: Hypothesis: capture is grabbing primary/default stream dependencies (memcpy/comm) and when instantiated those ops become serialized across GPUs because NCCL/IPC streams are tied to that captured sequence.

miguel: Quick experiment: try switching capture mode to CUDA_STREAM_CAPTURE_MODE_THREAD or capture only compute stream (avoid capturing the stream used for NCCL/memcpy). Also try inserting cudaStreamSynchronize after memcpys to see if explicit sync changes behavior (cheap but dirty test).

anna: Tried thread-capture: partial improvement, p50 drops to ~120ms but still higher than baseline. If I move memcpys to a dedicated stream and exclude it from capture, we get back to ~90ms.

jen: That suggests the memcpys/NCCL ordering is the problem. For Dedicated we should: 1) isolate NCCL + DMA streams from captured compute stream, 2) set stream capture to thread mode only when safe, 3) review our batching heuristics that changed when KV cache warmed.

kevin: Action items:
- anna: post the full nvtx timeline and the tiny repro harness (single script) so SRE can run locally.
- miguel: try creating a capture-aware stream allocator that reserves one stream for comm/dma and marks it NO_CAPTURE.
- jen: add a short test in nightly to turn off capture when KV cache ratio > 0.5 until we have a fix.

anna: Posting quick repro commands (run on 4xA10 testbed):
```bash
# warmup + reproduce
python repro_serving.py --gpus 0,1,2,3 --kv-warmup 50 --capture-mode global --batch-size 8
# profiler
nvprof --print-gpu-trace --events sync,memcpy -o profile.nvvp python repro_serving.py ...
```

kevin: Also add NCCL env dumps (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) when running, please.

miguel: If allocator approach works we can make it default: allocate comm stream pair per device and never include them in graph capture. That should restore comm/compute overlap.

anna: I'll upload nvvp and heap stats to the thread when I have them. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder — create a postmortem ticket if this blocks Dedicated customers.

kevin: I'll pick this up if anna is blocked on infra repros.

anna: Thanks, assigning to kevin if I can’t get a clean repro by EOD.

perf-bot: note: adding temp nightly guard (disable graph when kv_hit_rate > 0.6) increased cost by ~2% but removed the regression.

anna: End of thread for now — next will be kernel-level timeline with NVTX ranges to pinpoint exact op causing stalls.
